claims.claim_text: EDIT-401 is the company's lead in vivo development candidate, nominated September 2025; an IND or foreign equivalent is targeted by mid-2026 for HeFH hyperlipidemia.
claims.subject: EDIT-401
claims.source_quote: In September 2025, we announced the nomination of our lead in vivo development candidate, EDIT-401... We are on track to submit an investigational new drug application (IND) or foreign equivalent to conduct a clinical trial of EDIT-401 in patients with heterozygous familial hypercholesteremia (HeFH)... by mid-2026.

claims.claim_text: Reni-cel (renizgamglogene autogedtemcel), the former ex vivo gene-edited sickle cell / TDT program, was discontinued in December 2024.
claims.subject: reni-cel
claims.source_quote: we determined in December 2024 not to pursue commercialization for reni-cel in order to optimize our cost structure and accelerate our intent to achieve human proof of concept of our in vivo gene editing medicines.

claims.claim_text: Collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb (Juno Therapeutics) has produced 14 total programs, including BMS CD19 HD Allo CAR T in Phase 1 clinical development.
claims.subject: BMS_Juno_collaboration
claims.source_quote: our collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb Company (BMS) through its wholly owned subsidiary, Juno Therapeutics... has resulted in 14 total programs, including BMS CD19 HD Allo CAR T program for the treatment of autoimmune disease currently in Phase I clinical development.

claims.claim_text: Vertex License Agreement signed December 2023: Vertex obtained a non-exclusive license to Editas's Cas9 IP for BCL11A-targeting ex vivo therapies (covering Casgevy / exa-cel); Editas received $50.0M upfront in Q4 2023 and $10.0M annual license fee in Q1 2024, with future fees of $5.0-$40.0M per year through 2034.
claims.subject: Vertex_License_Agreement
claims.source_quote: In December 2023, we and Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated entered into a license agreement... Vertex obtained a non-exclusive license for our Cas9 gene editing technology for ex vivo gene editing medicines targeting the BCL11A gene in the fields of SCD and TDT, including Vertex's CASGEVY (exagamglogene autotemcel). We received a $50.0 million upfront cash payment in the fourth quarter of 2023 and the 2024 annual license fee of $10.0 million.

claims.claim_text: DRI Healthcare Trust agreement (October 2024): DRI paid Editas $57.0M upfront to purchase up to 100% of the future fixed and sales-based annual license fees under the Vertex License Agreement.
claims.subject: DRI_Healthcare_Trust
claims.source_quote: In October 2024, we entered into an agreement (the DRI Agreement) with a wholly owned subsidiary of DRI Healthcare Trust providing for an upfront cash payment by DRI to us of $57.0 million. Under the DRI Agreement, DRI is purchasing up to 100% of certain future fixed and sales-based annual license fees that the Company is entitled to receive under the Vertex License Agreement.

claims.claim_text: Editas owns or licenses foundational CRISPR/Cas9 and CRISPR/Cas12a (Cpf1) gene editing intellectual property, claiming to be the only human gene editing company with a platform covering both natural and engineered Cas9 and Cas12a.
claims.subject: Editas_CRISPR_IP
claims.source_quote: We believe we are the only human gene editing company with a platform that includes CRISPR/Cas9, CRISPR/Cas12a, engineered forms of both of these CRISPR systems, and foundational intellectual property for both of these CRISPR systems.

claims.claim_text: As of December 31, 2025, the company had $146.6M cash & cash equivalents (no marketable securities), with runway expected into Q3 2027; accumulated deficit of $1.6B and 2025 net loss of $160.1M.
claims.subject: Editas_liquidity
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $146.6 million... We expect that our existing cash and cash equivalents on December 31, 2025 will enable us to fund our operating expenses and capital expenditure requirements into the third quarter of 2027.

claims.claim_text: Cumulative payments received from BMS collaboration aggregate $159.0M (upfront, amendment, development milestones, research funding, opt-in fees); 2025 BMS collaboration revenue recognized was $23.2M; $44.5M deferred revenue remains at 12/31/2025.
claims.subject: BMS_collaboration_economics
claims.source_quote: In connection with our collaboration with BMS, we have received an aggregate of $159.0 million in payments... During the year ended December 31, 2025, we recognized $23.2 million of revenue related to our collaboration with BMS of which $9.7 million was previously deferred revenue. As of December 31, 2025, we had $40.5 million of deferred revenue related to BMS.
